utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. May I ask the registrar to call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. Case No. IT-04-80-I, the Prosecutor versus, Radivoje Miletic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, Mr. Miletic. Can you understand the proceedings? Can you hear me to start with?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear you and I can understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can we have the appearances now. Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, good morning Your Honour my name is Antoinette Issa. I'm here on behalf of the Prosecution, with Miss Stewart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And then for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Natacha Fauveau Ivanovic of the Paris bar, representing Mr. Miletic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Miletici as I already explained you already, last time, you have the right to remain silent which means that you don't have to say anything, no one can force you to do so. I would like to remind you that you are -- at your first initial appearance, you chose not to enter a plea of guilty or not guilty and we have, again, gathered today to enable you to plead. I will now produce to the -- to conduct the procedure part of this further initial appearance pursuant to Rule 62 of our Rules of Procedure and Evidence: First of all, Mr. Miletic, I have now to ensure that you are represented and I take note that you are represented by Miss Natacha Fauveau Ivanovic. Do you have anything to say in this respect?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I have not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: I take it that you have received the indictment in your own language.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: And do you understand its contents?

utterances.speaker: MS. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: May I explain the situation, Your Honour? I had to the opportunity to speak to the accused, my client, yesterday and as an example, I would like to tell you, that for instance, in paragraph 6 of the indictment, where is described the position of a General Miletici, in the French text as well as in the English text, we have three different positions. While in the Serbian language, there are four points. In paragraph 7, as described in the French text, it says that the Chief of Staff and in the Serbian, and it is the deputy Chief of Staff. There is also a problem with paragraph 34a. At a certain place in the French text -- in the English text they speak of a co-author and in Serbian it says an accomplice. There are other problems which I don't want to mention now. I have explained them to my client, but I hope he will get text in Serb which will be corrected. Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you. For the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We appreciate that he does understand the, according to counsel he does understand the indictment. And we will look into it and obviously resolve it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. Sir, I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Sorry. -- that despite these problems, which I hope soon, that you are ready to plead now. Okay. Then we can proceed with this. I first need to ensure that you waive your right to have the indictment read in full to you. As you know, under the Rules you have the right to have this done, but I understood that you waived this right. Can you confirm this to me, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Very well. So now I will proceed to this part of the proceeding, which will consist in the following. I will read out to you the five charges contained in the indictment and for each and any of the charges, I will ask you to tell me how do you plead to that charge, guilty or not guilty. Your answer, in each case, should be either guilty or not guilty and, as you probably know, in case you would fail to enter a plea, which I understand you won't, in that case I would enter a plea of not guilty on your behalf. May I ask you to stand up Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. now, Mr. Miletic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: The first count against you is a charge of murder, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(a) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plea, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: The second count against you is a charge of murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war punishable under Article 3 of the Statute. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: The third count against you is a charge of persecutions on political, racial and religious grounds, a crime against humanity, including murder, cruel and inhumane treatment, destruction of personal property, forcible transfer and deportation, punishable under Article 5 (h) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: The fourth count is a charge of inhumane acts, forcible transfer, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5 (i) of the Statute out of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: The fifth and last counts is a charge of deportation, a crime against humanity, punishable under article 5 (d) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down now, Mr. Miletic. Will the registrar please note that the accused has pleaded not guilty to all of the counts in the indictment. I must remind you, Mr. Miletic, that despite the fact that you have pleaded not guilty at this stage in the proceeding, that you retain the possibility to enter a guilty plea, so this you may do at a later stage, if you so wish. But now we proceed on the assumption that your plea is one of not guilty, which means that the further proceedings will be as follows: The registrar will fix a date for the trial when appropriate, but before that, we will have a status conference, which is to be held within 120 days after your first initial appearance, which should be somewhere in the beginning of July, as your first appearance was in the beginning of April. As you notice, the purpose of this status conference is two-fold. The first purpose is to organise the exchange between the parties and to facilitate the expeditious preparation for the trial. The second purpose is that I will have the opportunity to see you in person and to make sure that you are being treated well and to be made aware of any problems or requests that you may wish to make at that stage. And you will be informed of the exact date of that status conference in due course. Meanwhile, you will remain in custody, but, as you know, you may file an application for provisional release pursuant to Rule 65 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal and your Defence counsel can assist you with that, if necessary. The question of disclosure now. Pursuant to the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, the Prosecution must within 30 days of the initial appearance of the accused make available to the Defence counsel in a language which the accused understands all the supporting material which accompanied the indictment. For the reasons we discussed in our previous hearing, the time limit has been extended until the further initial appearance. Has the disclosure taken place or are you ready to do it now?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We are ready to do it now, and it is all complete and it's been translated and provided to counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: So this then can be taken care of after the hearing or now. I don't know how you want to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: It may be more expeditious to proceed after the hearing. We have briefly spoken to Defence counsel and I believe she is aware that we do have it for her to pick up any time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So at this stage I must remind the Defence the delay provided in Article 72 starts running. So as from now you have a delay of one month, again, to put forward any preliminary motions that you would wish to formulate under that Article of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Speaking about disclosure, now I turn to the Prosecution. Has the Prosecution submitted the Article 66 material to the other accused, Mr. Gvero? Has that happened?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we have provided that on the 5th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Okay. Would it be possible to file an official notification of that, because we haven't been officially notified of that disclosure. So if that could perhaps be done.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you. So I think that this is all for today. Is there any matter that the Prosecution wishes to raise at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No, not at this time, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you. And the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: General Miletic submitted a few motions regarding the lead counsel and consequently these motions are now moot. Therefore if any such motions are still pending with the Chamber, he withdraws them. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: If there are no further requests, we will now adjourn the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: adjourned at 10.47 a.m.
